title: Prompt Quality Workbench data
note: Clauses, the decision each clause removes from the model, and the generation failure modes (Chapter 5) that an open decision makes more likely. The links are a teaching heuristic, not measured probabilities.

failureModes.Hallucinated API: The model writes a call the library does not have. Symptom: a console error about an unknown function.
failureModes.Library version drift: Code and library release no longer match. Symptom: code that once worked errors or draws differently.
failureModes.Control in drawing area: A hard-coded y position puts a slider or button over the drawing.
failureModes.Non-responsive canvas: A hard-coded width and no updateCanvasSize(), so the canvas ignores window resizes.
failureModes.Wrong iframe height: The iframe height differs from the canvas height plus 2, so controls are clipped in the chapter.
failureModes.Text with an outline: A stroke is still active when text() runs, so labels look fuzzy or heavy.
failureModes.Unrequested extra files: The model helpfully regenerates files you did not ask for, and each one is extra review work (see the tip 'Name the Output You Do Not Want').
failureModes.Spec and sim disagree: The model fills a gap with its own guess, so the MicroSim no longer matches its specification block (see Iterative Refinement).

clauses.name: Skill
clauses.title: Names the skill
clauses.text: Use the microsim-generator skill to create the MicroSim
clauses.example: "Use the microsim-generator skill to create the MicroSim ..." Invoking the skill loads its p5.js guide and template, so conventions such as updateCanvasSize() and noStroke() before text() arrive with it.
clauses.decision: Which conventions and template to follow

clauses.name: Spec
clauses.title: Points to the specification
clauses.text: specified in the block with sim-id {simId} in {chapter}.
clauses.example: "... specified in the block with sim-id pendulum-period-explorer in docs/chapters/[chapter]/index.md." The block carries the objective, the controls, every range and every default.
clauses.decision: Which controls, ranges and defaults to build

clauses.name: Version pin
clauses.title: Pins the library version
clauses.text: Use the pinned library version in the skill's main.html template.
clauses.example: "Use the pinned library version in the skill's main.html template." Naming the pin tells the model which release to write for, for example p5.js 2.x with no preload().
clauses.decision: Which library version to write for

clauses.name: Output files
clauses.title: Limits the output files
clauses.text: Generate only the JavaScript file; the scaffold already exists.
clauses.example: "Generate only the JavaScript file; the scaffold already exists." This keeps the scaffolded main.html, index.md and metadata.json, with their iframe height, untouched.
clauses.decision: Which files to create or overwrite

clauses.name: Layout
clauses.title: States the layout
clauses.example: "Layout: drawing region above a control region; canvas 400 wide by 450 high." Stating the regions and sizes fixes where controls go and how tall the canvas is.
clauses.decision: Where controls go and how tall the canvas is

clauses.name: Tie-break
clauses.title: Gives a tie-breaking rule
clauses.text: If the specification and the skill's conventions conflict, stop and ask me.
clauses.example: "If the specification and the skill's conventions conflict, stop and ask me." Without it the model settles every conflict silently and you find out only when you test.

scenarios.label: Easy: bouncing ball, one slider
scenarios.request: Make a bouncing ball simulation with a speed slider.
scenarios.layout: drawing region 400 high above one 50-pixel control row
scenarios.why: A one-slider sketch is close to the template, so most gaps are cheap to fix.

scenarios.label: Medium: pendulum period explorer
scenarios.layout: drawing region above a control region; canvas 400 wide by 450 high
scenarios.why: The length range 0.2 to 2.0 and the period readout live only in the specification, and without a named pin the model may write p5.js 1.x code, such as preload(), for the skill's 2.3.2 template.

scenarios.label: Hard: projectile lab with a live chart
scenarios.request: Make a projectile lab with a chart of range against angle.
scenarios.layout: simulation left, range chart right; three slider rows below drawHeight
scenarios.why: Two panels, three sliders and a chart give the model many places to guess.
